notes:
A clean eight-bullet ladder that crosses eras: present-day Jeuno, then Southern San d'Oria (S) and the Eldieme Necropolis (S). ZERO EVIDENCE anywhere and that is correct -- nothing is handed to you mid-mission; the Hi-Elixir and Chac-chacs are Reward, which proves the mission is over rather than that a step is done. Bullet 1 is the page's own '(Optional)' Elijah visit and is kept as an optional rung: the rendered bullet loses what it was for ('for .', an image the prepass could not render) and the Notes section says the same NPC opens two Records of Eminence objectives, so it is a side visit the page endorses, not a ladder position. Bullet 6 is ONE step, not two: you check the Egg Discovery Site to open the battle, so the trigger and the fight are the same targetable location and splitting them would only add a rung nothing can observe. The three saplings Enkelados brings are deliberately NOT in `mobs` -- 'Sapling' is a world-wide monster name and a live mob match on it would draw a marker on any sapling anywhere; the named three are enough. The real unmodellable gate is NPC availability: Valaineral is a Campaign NPC who can be out of town, and the Egg Discovery Site refuses to fire if Noillurie (M-7/8) is injured or on a Campaign Operation. Neither is observable, so the ladder just points at them.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 1: What it is for is lost in rendering ('for .'); the Notes section says Elijah near Home Point #1 opens two Records of Eminence objectives.

the cutscene that begins the mission
a Campaign NPC: he may be away at battle, and zoning out and back can be needed once he returns. Voucheramme, Hinrich or Dallus-Mallus track the Royal Guards.
the shiny Secret Entrance at the eastern edge of (G-7); touching it puts you in The Eldieme Necropolis (S). The Survival Guide or Campaign Warp lands close.
the site refuses if Noillurie (M-7/8) is injured or conducting a Campaign Operation, and it tells you so. Not observable from here.

check the site a second time to open the battle -- trigger and fight are the same location. 15 minute limit. Enkelados brings 3 Saplings, left out of the mob list on purpose because 'Sapling' matches monsters all over the world. The RNG spawns on the ledge and must be pulled down, or fight from up there.
after winning, for another cutscene
final cutscene and rewards

notes: Five bullets, four steps, and one genuine evidence point. Bullets 2 and 3 are one step: the page says outright that the fight starts the instant you select the Bibliomaniac's Lair, so an examine rung in front of it would be a rung no player ever stands on -- bullet 3 is the roster and a sleepable/silenceable note. The [KI] Liber Daemonium at bullet 4 IS evidence: it is handed over at that step, and the header's Reward is 20,000 Gil, so the key item is not a completion token. Step 4 reuses the (F-10) grid the page gave Andreine in bullet 1 -- same NPC, same zone, one page.

steps.note: the receptionist on the left as you enter

selecting the Lair starts the fight instantly and clears any Velkk aggro. Route: Waypoint #2, southeast to the watch tower, tunnel NE at (J-9/10), then at the tent/reive take the cave on the left and climb the vine; the Lair is on flat rock in front of the Seat of Gramk-Droog.
after the fight; the key item arrives after the cutscene
final cutscene and reward; the grid is bullet 1's, the page gives none here

notes: Six bullets, five steps. Bullet 5 ('you will enter a cutscene after the fight') is an outcome, not a rung, and folds into the fight's note. Bullets 3 and 4 are kept apart even though both touch the Test of Talents, because the first is a cutscene and the second enters the battlefield -- same marker either way, so the extra rung costs nothing and keeps the page auditable. NO EVIDENCE: Oshasha's Treatise is the header Reward, so it proves the mission is over rather than that a step is done, and nothing else is handed over. The last step is Andreine in the Celennia Memorial Library and the page gives no grid for her here; 9-1's page puts her at (F-10) but that is a different page, so this one keeps null rather than importing it.

steps.note: near Home Point #2; the grid is the walkthrough's, the header names none
nearby the Odyssean Passage

touch it again for a SOLO battlefield: you must be disbanded with no party member in the zone, and trusts are barred. Buffs that survive zoning carry in. Volker, Zeid, Valli, Oshasha and Romaa Mihgo assist and losing all five is an automatic loss. Bullet 5 is the post-fight cutscene, an outcome rather than a step.
final cutscene and reward; this page gives no grid for her

notes: The mission ENDS at bullet 6. Bullet 7 ('continue with the creation of your Prime Weapon') and both of the long After-the-walkthrough sections -- 'Starting your Prime Weapon' (Oggbi, then Gama-Shama for 10k Gallimaufry) and 'A Word on Choosing Your Weapon' -- are what you do AFTER the reward, so none of them are steps here even though the page renders them as bullets. They matter later: TVR 10-5 will not start without an upgraded Prime Weapon equipped, which is why the exclusion is flagged rather than silent. Bullets 4 and 5 merge -- the travel to Outer Ra'Kaznar (K-3) exists only to reach the Shrouded Workroom at (K-3), one place, one rung, and the do-not-touch-the-roots warning rides in the note. Bullet 1 is the page's own '(Optional)' hint and is also the header's Start NPC, so the giver stays Andreine either way. The one evidence point is [KI] Bronze-hued tag at bullet 3: obtained at that step and NOT in Reward (Reward is the [KI] Silver Knife membership card plus the ability to start Prime Weapons, both of which prove the mission is over).

steps.note: the page's own '(Optional)': a hint about Oshasha's whereabouts. Also the header's Start NPC.
Stygian Ash drops from the Pixie family around Witchfire Glen in Grauberg (S); the sub-bullets are routes to get there and are not steps.
Upper Floor, map 1. Bullet 4 is the journey to the same (K-3) so it merges. DO NOT interact with the roots at (J-3) on the way or you are teleported back to the entrance. Umbrils patrol the area.
final cutscene and reward; the mission ends here

notes: Seventeen top-level bullets, four steps. The mission is bullets 1-7 and finishes at the automatic cutscene in bullet 7, which is an outcome and not a rung. BULLETS 8-17 ARE A DIFFERENT PROCEDURE ENTIRELY -- 'To unlock the Proto-Waypoint' -- a walk through Newton Movalpolos trading Firesand to a furnace to open a gate, ending at a Geomagnetic Fount. It is a convenience unlock done after the mission, and its own text gives it away: bullet 9 pays Twinkbrix 2,716 gil where the mission's bullet 4 pays him 10k for the same warp, so the two are not describing the same act. Putting any of it in the ladder would send a player on a long detour the mission never asks for. Bullet 3 is travel advice for reaching Tarnotik and merges into step 2. NO EVIDENCE: nothing is handed over, the Reward is gil, and the Snow Lily / 10k gil warps are optional transport rather than requirements, so they stay in notes and out of `items`.

steps.note: Home Point #3; inside a house on the upper walkway, in the back room
bullet 3 is only how to get there: the Proto-Waypoint warp lands at (K-10), or the Movalpolos Survival Guide.
getting there: trade Tarnotik a Snow Lily, take the Newton Movalpolos Home Point, or pay Twinkbrix 10k gil. None of those is required, so none is in `items`.

interact with the entrance again and pick 'To Movalpolos!'. Trusts allowed. Ariri Samariri has Death. Jabbos assists and engages the moment you draw, whatever the distance. Bullet 7 is the automatic cutscene and reward.

notes: Four rungs, all on one NPC, alternating talk and trade -- which is exactly what the page describes and why no rung is dropped: the trades are the acts, the talks pick the dialogue option that unlocks them. Bullet 1 is shopping advice, not a step; its two items become the `items` of the trades that spend them, and it is cited on both. NO EVIDENCE: nothing is handed to you, the Reward is gil, and 'you traded a humus' is not observable. THE ONE REAL HAZARD IS THE NPC ITSELF -- the page says there are TWO places at (F-4) holding a Mandragora Warden and only the one entered from (E-4) is right (it has a single Warden). The name is what chronicle already ships for this row so the marker does not move, but a player following it may still stand at the wrong (F-4); that is why it is flagged rather than buried. The 'for each member of your party' line is party-sized and cannot be expressed as a count, so `count` stays 1 -- one per player is what one player must hold.

start.raw: Mandragora Warden, The Boyahda Tree Map 1 (F-4)

steps.note: Map 1, and ask about Magh Bihu. TWO spots at (F-4) hold a Mandragora Warden; the correct one is entered from (E-4) and has only a single Warden. Proto-Waypoint is closest, else the Home Point near the Cloister and north to exit F, or Unity Warp 135.

bullet 1 is where to get it: Gancanagh in Abyssea - Tahrongi (spawned by trading Alkaline Humus to the ??? at the east of (H-8)), or the auction house under Others -> Misc. 2. Bullet 1 says one per party member; the count here is what one player holds.
select 'Where did Magh Bihu go?'
final cutscene and reward. Bullet 1: Watermelon is sold by Scamplix near Home Point #2 in Rabao (F-7).

notes: Three bullets, three steps, and the shortest mission in the lane. Bullet 1 IS a step, unusually: it is not shopping advice but a farm with a zone, a grid, a named monster and a hard count -- six Fat Worm Meat off Boulder Eaters in Gustav Tunnel (J-6), Map 2 -- and the item is Exclusive, so it cannot be bought and the farm cannot be skipped. Holding six of them is the one thing here a packet can see, so it is step 1's evidence: obtained AT that step, and the Reward ([KI] Sheet of Destiny Destroyer tunes, gil) is untouched by it. The same six then appear as step 3's `items`, which is the requirement to trade rather than a second evidence claim -- evidence appears exactly once, on the earlier step. Note the count is 6 and not 1: the trade wants all six.

steps.note: Map 2; Unity Warp 128 lands on the right map. Treasure Hunter helps and the drop rate is low. Fat Worm Meat is Exclusive, so it cannot be bought -- this rung is not optional.

Map 4, the same map Juggler Hecatomb spawns on; he stands in the middle of the room behind a shed. Survival Guide then exit A, keep left and down tunnel G; or tunnel B, tunnel E, west to drop H on Map 3.
all six, for the cutscene and reward

notes: Six bullets, five steps; bullet 6 is the exit into Xarcabard and the reward, an outcome. Bullet 2 is a real rung even though it names no entity: ZONING into Mine Shaft #2716 is what fires the cutscene, so it is a travel step targeting the zone rather than an examine on an invented object -- the Shaft Entrance the previous mission used is not named here. The Throne Room step's ZONE comes from a sub-bullet ('Home Point warp to Castle Zvahl Keep is closest'), which is the only place the page names it; the target keeps the page's own wording, 'Throne Room door'. NO EVIDENCE: nothing is handed over at any step and the Reward is gil.

steps.note: the Proto-Waypoint warp lands at (K-10); otherwise the Oldton Movalpolos Survival Guide.
entering the zone is what triggers the cutscene. Tarnotik warps you for a Snow Lily, Twinkbrix for 10k gil, or take the Newton Movalpolos Home Point -- all optional, so none is in `items`.
back to him for another cutscene
the zone is named only in this bullet's sub-bullet ('Home Point warp to Castle Zvahl Keep is closest'), and the target keeps the page's wording. No grid is given.

click the door again to enter the battlefield. Each foe carries an aura (Blind, Addle, Slow) that lifts when it dies, and all can be silenced and slept. Magh Bihu and Dazbog assist and engage when you draw.

notes:
The start is a TARGETABLE LOCATION, not a person: Heroes' Gambit at Xarcabard (J-9), which is also what chronicle ships for this row, so the giver is unchanged and the same location closes the mission at bullet 5. THE GATE THIS MISSION CANNOT EXPRESS is bullet 1's 'equip your upgraded Prime Weapon': the page names no weapon, only the two that do NOT count (Duban and Loughnashade), and the Prime Weapon is chosen from a list back in mission 9-4. An `items` entry would have to invent a name, so `items_partial` carries the fact that a requirement exists that could not be written -- and the note says which. [KI] Despairing psyche is recorded as step 5's `items` and NOT as evidence: the page says you LOSE it there, which means you must be holding it, but it never says where in this mission it was granted, and inventing an evidence step for it would place the mark on a rung the page does not describe. Bullet 4 (moved to Xarcabard after the cutscene) is a transition and merges into step 4.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 1: hence items_partial.

steps.note: Requires an upgraded Prime Weapon EQUIPPED. The page names none of the weapons that qualify, only that Duban and Loughnashade are excluded, so the requirement cannot be written as an item list Unity warp 125 lands close.
directly across from the Home Point; the Rift is not visible until the story reaches this point

interact again to enter the battlefield. 15 minute limit. The Destiny Destroyers assist and the fight ends the moment one of them dies, so keep reraise up. Chaos dispels everything including stances and gear. The page notes that any weapon damages him despite the lore, and that you may change job after the pre-fight cutscene.

bullet 4 puts you back in Xarcabard after the cutscene, so it merges here. The reward is gil and the [KI] Despairing psyche is taken from you; holding it is therefore a requirement of this rung, but the page never says which step granted it, so it is not used as evidence.

notes: The richest ladder in the lane and the only one with a group. Bullet 3 is FOUR steps, not one: the page gives four fixed Twinkling Presence locations in Dynamis - Xarcabard and says only 'collect four other shards scattered around the zone', so they are an unordered set sharing the group 'shards' and all four draw at once. THE EVIDENCE SITS ON THE LAST GROUP MEMBER AND LISTS ALL FOUR PSYCHES, for the same reason An Explorer's Footsteps does it: the page names the four key items but never says which shard gives which, so per-shard evidence would be invented, and an AND-list of all four on the last member is true exactly when the group is finished -- which is the condition the ladder actually needs. Bullet 1 is a precondition nothing can observe (you must change areas after the previous mission or the Twinkling Presence will not appear) and folds into step 1's note. Two more honest evidence points: [KI] Despairing psyche at bullet 2 and [KI] Raebrimm's memento at bullet 4, both handed over at their own step, and neither is the Reward (Cornelia's Belt). The After-the-walkthrough Notes section is the standard Elijah Records of Eminence line and is not a step.

steps.note: bullet 1 is a precondition folded in here: you must change areas after finishing the previous mission or the Twinkling Presence will not be visible. Nothing observes that. The grid is the header's.
NW section of (I-9), in the flat area surrounded by demons. Fixed location; any order.
east side of (H-7), on top of the right-hand cliff visible while walking up the ramp
north middle of (F-7), above where Xarcabard's zone line to Uleguerand Range is

NW corner of (G-10). LAST member of the group, which is why it carries the evidence for all four shards: the page never says which Presence gives which psyche, so holding all four is the only honest reading of 'the group is done'.
the glowing targetable location where the Dynamis Lord fight is; only clickable once all four shards are collected
cutscene and reward

notes: Five bullets, four steps; bullet 5 is the automatic cutscene and reward, an outcome. THE START IS A MOOGLE IN YOUR OWN MOG HOUSE, which is the most delicate thing on the page: 'Moogle' is one of the resolver's known-ambiguous names -- it matches every Moogle in Vana'diel -- and an ambiguous NPC with no zone is a structural refusal. So step 1 carries the zone 'Mog House', which the resolver answers with its moghouse sentinel rather than a zone id, and that is what keeps the step from matching everywhere. The name itself is chronicle's own, so the giver does not move. Step 2's target is a literal '???' and can never carry a marker; it keeps its rung because the ladder position is real even when the marker is not, and the note says the page calls it the Stone Circle. Steps 3 and 4 are both the Moogle Meeting -- cutscene then battlefield -- so one marker serves both. NO EVIDENCE: nothing is handed over before the Plat. Mog. Belt, which is the Reward.

steps.note: your own Moogle, in the Mog House of your home nation -- which nation that is varies per character. The zone is the Mog House sentinel, not a world zone.
the Stone Circle; the page names the target only as the ??? targetable location, so the rung keeps its place and loses its marker. UNM 99 warp to La Theine Plateau is the quickest route.
reached by exiting Ordelle's Caves Map 3 near Morbolger (path B, then D, then drop the southeast hole at (H-11) on Map 2), or the Proto-Waypoint to La Theine Plateau.
interact again to enter the instanced battlefield. Trusts allowed; all four can be slept and silenced. Bullet 5 is the winning cutscene and reward.
